title: The Deadline Draft: Speak-Up Variant
brief: At Meridian Advisory a valuation report for a client is due by 5 p.m. The peer review left 4 open comments, including a figure that does not agree with its source. An analyst reports that the engagement partner asked them to sign the review checklist as complete so the report can be issued. This is a 2026 variant on quality culture and speaking up. It is preliminary and excluded from badge scoring and the capstone until verified. You have 12 visit points to gather what you need and make a decision you can justify.

actions.label: General state of the file
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Engagement partner: what was asked of the analyst
Analysts: what they would do if asked to sign an incomplete review
Concern log and a word with the analysts

evidence.text: Review checklist {{lot}}: the peer review lists 4 open comments, one on a figure of 2.4 million that does not match the source workbook; the checklist is signed complete at 14:20 and the report status is ready to issue.
evidence.whyItMatters: A report is issued only when the planned review shows it is right, or when an authorized person approves. A checklist signed complete with open comments bypasses the review. This 2015 requirement is reported to continue in intent; any change in the 2026 wording is unclear.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the open comments with the checklist signature and time.

evidence.text: The source workbook is version-controlled; its last change, version 12, is recorded with author and date.
evidence.whyItMatters: The source is controlled, so the mismatch points to the report, not the workbook.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: the data behind the result is sound.

evidence.text: Engagement partner: "Sign it off; I'll deal with the comments in the next version. The client is expecting it today." The partner says the same was done on 2 earlier reports.
evidence.whyItMatters: The 2026 edition is reported to add a requirement for top management to promote and demonstrate a quality culture and ethical behavior (5.1.1). Pressure from a leader to change a result or skip a check works against it. Acting on a failed check is already a 2015 requirement.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask the person who applies the pressure what they asked for, and compare it with the release rule.

evidence.text: Analyst interviews: 2 of 3 analysts asked did not know they could decline to sign a review checklist, or whom to tell. Induction record IN-7 covers templates and confidentiality only.
evidence.whyItMatters: Awareness is reported to extend to the organization's quality culture and ethical behavior (7.3). People need to know the route for raising a concern and that they may use it.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask frontline staff what they would do, and whom they would tell, if a check failed near a deadline.

evidence.text: The concern log shows 0 entries in 22 weeks. An analyst says a colleague who declined to sign a review last year was left off the next engagement.
evidence.whyItMatters: A note on the environment for operation of processes (7.1.4) is reported to recognize that culture can influence operating conditions. Silence after an earlier report was met badly is a sign that the environment discourages reporting. Recorded as an observation because the 2026 wording is unverified.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the concern or near-miss log with what staff say in interview. The gap is the evidence.

evidence.text: Issue log: no entry for the 4 open review comments. The last entry, IL-33, is 8 weeks old.
evidence.whyItMatters: Open review comments on an issued report need a record so they can be resolved and traced. A missing entry means no one owns the correction.
evidence.missedExplanation: The procedure names the log. Follow the trail from the procedure to the record.

evidence.text: Quality procedure QM-3 says a report is issued only after all review comments are closed or accepted in writing by the quality partner. The quality partner is in the office until 6 p.m.
evidence.whyItMatters: The organization has a defined route, with named authority, for this exact situation.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: a sound route exists. The risk is in bypassing it.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The procedure is sound and the named person is available. Conforming.

evidence.text: Recognition note RN-1: 2 months ago the managing partner thanked a junior analyst in writing for stopping a report that used a superseded rate table. The stop and its outcome are logged.
evidence.whyItMatters: Thanking a person who stopped work, and recording the outcome, shows leaders supporting the behavior that 5.1.1 is reported to expect.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: a sign of the culture the organization wants.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A recognized stop-work event is good practice, not an issue.

evidence.text: The team calendar shows the client deadline as 5 p.m. today.
evidence.whyItMatters: A plan shown on a board is communication, not a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The board shows the plan. A deadline on display is not evidence of a breach.

evidence.text: A working paper has one figure struck through with a single line, initialled and dated, with the correct figure beside it.
evidence.whyItMatters: A correction that leaves the original legible, with initials and date, protects the integrity of the record.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A single-line correction with initials and date is good record practice. Conforming.

evidence.text: Partner meeting minutes of 5 September list 6 utilization and billing measures and no item on concerns raised or how they were handled.
evidence.whyItMatters: Leaders are reported to need to demonstrate a quality culture with evidence (5.1.1). A review meeting is one place to show it. This is an observation, not a nonconformity: commentary says no separate culture program is required, so avoid audit criteria the standard may not state.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read what leaders review. What is never discussed is rarely managed.

decisions.prompt: The partner asks the analyst to sign now. What do you advise?
options: Sign the checklist; the partner takes responsibility
Do not sign; tell the quality partner now and propose closing the figure comment first, then sending the report by 6 p.m. or a clearly marked draft with the client's agreement
Ask another analyst to sign instead
decisions.rationale: The quality partner is available and the figure can be checked today. Speaking up through the named route is the behavior that 5.1.1 is reported to ask leaders to make easy.
optionFeedback: Signing an incomplete review misreports it, whoever asks.
This is proportionate, uses the named authority, and keeps the client informed.
A week-long delay is disproportionate when the comments can be closed today.
A different signature does not close the comments.

decisions.prompt: The analyst who reported the request is concerned about future work allocation. What should the managing partner do?
options: Tell the analyst that partners decide sign-off
Wait to see whether the client complains
Discuss it only at the year-end appraisal
Thank the analyst, confirm that reporting was right, review the sign-off practice as a system issue, and make sure work allocation is not affected
decisions.rationale: Leaders are reported to need to promote and demonstrate a quality culture (5.1.1). Protecting the reporter and changing the practice is the evidence an auditor would look for.

containment: Withdraw the signature on checklist {{lot}} and hold the report until the comments are closed or accepted by the quality partner
correction: Correct the 2.4 million figure against the source workbook and close the other comments before issue
cause: Deadline pressure was allowed to override the review rule, and analysts were not made aware of, or supported in using, the route for raising concerns
corrective: Leaders state and show that open comments stop issue; add raising concerns to the induction; block report issue while review comments are open
effectiveness: For the next quarter, sample issued reports monthly for open comments at issue and review concerns raised and responses at the partner meeting

debriefText.found: You kept the true result, used the defined route, and treated the pressure as a system condition rather than a personal failing.
debriefText.missed: In a culture case, compare what the records say with what people say in interview. Leaders' responses to earlier reports are part of the evidence.
debriefText.falseFinding: A deadline on a board and a properly corrected record are normal. They show planning and good record practice, not a weak culture.

bridge2026.text: Top management is reported to be required to promote and demonstrate a quality culture and ethical behavior. In this case, look at how partners respond when a review is incomplete near a deadline.
Awareness is reported to extend to the organization's quality culture and ethical behavior, so staff should know how to raise a concern and that they may do so.
A note on the environment for operation of processes is reported to recognize that culture and ethical behavior can influence operating conditions.
An auditor checking culture is likely to examine decisions, records of concerns raised, and how leaders responded, rather than attitudes or a separate culture program.
bridge2026.reasoning: Sources describe culture as shown through behavior and evidence, and commentary says no separate culture program is required.
bridge2026.check: Read 5.1.1, its note, and the Annex A guidance on culture in the purchased 2026 text, and ask the certification body how it will audit culture.

bridge2026.text: Release of products and services is reported as carried forward in intent from 2015; any change in wording is unclear.
